targetTest: an entry with an invalid asset ref never reaches the read port and is marked unavailable
expected: loadProjectBrushSet lists every well-formed tip of the pack, healthy or not: an unavailable tip keeps its entry with digest/mask null so the library can grey it (D-18), it is added to unavailableTipIds, and the failure carries the precise reason (missing / unreadable / wrong-size / digest-mismatch / refused for native results, invalid-asset-ref for a malformed or absent asset ref — never sent to the read port, batch-failed when the whole read is refused). A record whose only carrier violation is its asset ref is recovered as a tip (asset dropped) so it can be listed; three failures collapse into ONE aggregate unavailable state naming three ids; the open never throws and no mask is ever fabricated.
actual: The RED run executed all 26 assertions across the two files: 6 new loader assertions fail while the 3 opening/source-order pins and the full 17-assertion catalog suite stay green. Task 1 healthy-only semantics surfaced exactly as expected: a refused batch listed 0 entries instead of 2, a single failed entry listed 1 of 2, a digest mismatch listed 0 of 1, a valid record without an asset listed 0 of 1, the aggregate-three case listed 1 of 4, and the invalid-asset-ref record was neither listed nor sent to unavailableTipIds (the id join came back empty string instead of wc/custom-bad in the first capture; the corrected assertion now shows the entry list as wc/custom-ok instead of wc/custom-bad,wc/custom-ok). The round-fallback catalog pin passes already by construction because registry absence alone yields the neutral preset — the production change is confined to listing and reason reporting.
semanticAssessment: The target test executed and failed on its planned assertion: "expected 'wc/custom-ok' to be 'wc/custom-bad,wc/custom-ok'". Six loader tests failed and all other 20 assertions passed in the same run; no file failed to load or collect, and no failure is an import, syntax, setup or fixture fault. One assertion authored in the first RED pass contradicted the plan law that unavailable entries stay listed; it was corrected before GREEN (entries now expect wc/custom-bad first with a null mask) and the RED capture was re-run, still failing for the same planned behavior gap: loadProjectBrushSet drops unavailable tips from entries instead of listing them with digest/mask null, and cannot represent a listed-but-unavailable tip. The catalog round-fallback pin is a regression guard for D-21/D-22, green at RED because it pins existing registry-absence behavior.
